Ms. Budge acknowledged Ms. Clark and the local Carson City Bee Campus and noted that financial contributions for pollinator efforts could be made through donations to the Foundation for Carson City Parks and Recreation. records.sourceSnippet: roll call vote, the motion carried unanimously. Chair Brooks, Vice Chair Goodman, and Regents Arrascada, Bautista, Boylan, Brager, Brown, Carvalho, Del Carlo, Downs, Fernandez, Goicoechea and McGrath voted yes. GBC Interim President Donnelli requested that everyone offer an act of kindness today because although people cannot ease the pain of the world, it can be honored by choosing compassion. The Board discussed strategic priorities supported by its work, including accessibility improvements, public safety, ADA compliance, audible pedestrian signals, multimodal transportation, and bicycle and pedestrian safety. Members also identified emerging concerns related to e-bikes, transit accessibility, and gaps in bus service coverage, particularly in northwest Reno. The Board discussed potential recommendations for inclusion in the annual report, including continued investment in accessibility improvements, improved transit access, and ongoing collaboration with RTC to address safety and mobility needs.
